ghost's verdier barrel exports a `FOUR` constant ([F.BOT, F.T, F.F, F.TOP]); metrologic renamed the identical array to `GAUGE_ORDER` (to avoid colliding with chu's own differently-shaped `FOUR`). Same value, different export name -- a ghost consumer importing `{ FOUR }` from verdier gets `undefined` from metrologic and must import `GAUGE_ORDER` instead. All other verdier exports (GAUGE, abelianize, charPoly, colimStructure, determinant, firingPatternSelfDual, fixedPointClosure, fixedSet, inducedPermutation, isPisot, isPrimitive, iterate, matEqual, matmul, orbit, perronConvergent, perronPoly, rank, smithNormalForm, stepNInvariant, substitute, substitutionRuleSelfDual, transpose, verdierDual, verdierHolds) are identical, both name and (per code diff) semantics.

export name and the other exports (regimeOfOrdinal, leastFixedPoint, OMEGA, OMEGA_SQ, etc.) are unchanged, but metrologic's closureOrdinal return object gained a `least: boolean` field that the ghost's version does not have. Metrologic tracks whether a search block was exhausted without finding a fixed point (`skippedGap`); if a later ordinal is found fixed after such a gap, it reports `least: false` because that gap could hide the true least fixed point, whereas the ghost always implicitly claims leastness. This is an additive, non-breaking correctness enrichment (existing `{kappa,value,regime}` consumers, e.g. `leastFixedPoint` which only reads `.value`, are unaffected), but it is a real behavioral divergence for any ghost consumer that inspects the full closureOrdinal() return shape.

limits: Coverage is NOT fully 'covered': verdier has a renamed export (FOUR -> GAUGE_ORDER, same value) and closure's closureOrdinal has a diverged return shape (metrologic adds a `least: boolean` field). Per instructions, the deprecation signpost (npm deprecate) was therefore SKIPPED -- coverage is incomplete, not clean equality plus purely-additive modules.

Registry reachability was checked as an informational aside only (curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4873/-/ping returned {} -- registry is up), but the deprecation command itself was not run because of the coverage gap above, not because of registry/auth availability.

Export-name comparison was done via a regex-based static extractor (export {..}/export function/export const/export * as) run against both trees' source files, not via a live import/runtime introspection; template-literal or computed export patterns, if any existed, would not be caught (none were observed in either tree).

'diverged-semantics' scope was limited to a textual diff of every shared .mjs/.d.ts file after stripping @561-group/math <-> @lenticule-science/metrologic string substitutions; only closure/src/closure.mjs and verdier/src/{index,gauge}.mjs had non-cosmetic diffs. All other shared files diffed as identical apart from the package-name string.

The revival backlog was scoped to files actually importing an @561-group/math subpath (or declaring it as a package.json dependency); package-lock-only or comment-only mentions were excluded and logged separately under outOfScopeFindings. The vendored inline copy under education-platform-service/web/js/vendor/math/ has no package.json and so is not part of the package-repoint backlog, only listed for awareness.

The two 'computer' kernel/vfs snapshots (lib/legacy/computer/ and lib/legacy/2026-06-17-computer/) are near-identical duplicate trees of 18 micro-packages each; only the dated snapshot's package.json pins an exact ghost version (0.0.1) where the undated one uses workspace:*. Per-subpackage import usage was checked once against the undated tree and assumed identical for the dated snapshot (spot confirmed by diff -rq showing only package.json version-string differences and missing AGENTS.md files, no source divergence).
